title: Deploy an AI service with confidence
description: Package, release, monitor, and recover a small AI application.
prerequisites: API integration and basic terminal usage.
objectives: Define health, release, and rollback checks
explanation: Deployment turns a local experiment into a service with an owner. A container image packages application files and dependencies; a running container is an instance of that image. Keep secrets and deployment-specific configuration outside the image. A container improves packaging consistency, but it does not by itself provide secure or reliable operations.

A delivery pipeline should check the application, build an identifiable artifact, and deploy it in a controlled way. Include AI evaluation in release criteria when prompts, models, or retrieval behavior change. Keep a known working version and the configuration needed to restore it.

Scaling must account for provider limits as well as your own servers. Add bounded queues, request limits, timeouts, and cost budgets. Monitor service health and user-visible outcomes. A process being alive is not the same as the service being able to answer useful requests.

terms.definition: A packaged template used to create containers.

example: Release a policy assistant to a small internal group first. Watch error rates, latency, retrieval quality, and cost. If a new prompt increases unsupported answers beyond the agreed threshold, restore the previous prompt and application configuration.
mistakes: Scaling workers beyond provider rate limits.
Changing prompts without versioning or evaluation.
exercise: Write a deployment checklist with a readiness check, a small initial rollout, three monitored metrics, and a concrete rollback trigger.

questions.question: How does an image differ from a container?
questions.answer: An image is the packaged template; a container is a running instance created from that template.
questions.distractor: They are always the same running process.

questions.question: Where should deployment secrets be supplied?
questions.answer: At runtime through a controlled secret mechanism or server environment, not baked into the image or source repository.
questions.distractor: Inside the public Dockerfile as literal values.

questions.question: More workers trigger provider rate limits. What should you add?
questions.answer: Coordinate concurrency with provider limits using bounded queues, throttling, and appropriate retry behavior.

questions.question: Why version prompts alongside releases?
questions.answer: Prompt changes can alter behavior; versioning makes evaluation, attribution, and rollback possible.

questions.question: What is a useful rollback trigger?
questions.answer: A predefined breach in a user-relevant metric, such as unsupported-answer rate or error rate, with an owner and restore procedure.
questions.distractor: Any change in the color of the dashboard.
